content.title: About
content.content: Cape Cod is a soft cheese with a buttery flavor and a hint of tang, made from whole cow’s milk sourced from pastures in New England. The cheese has a creamy texture, a slightly crumbly rind, and a golden‑yellow interior. It is commonly used in sandwiches, salads, and as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese is named after the Cape Cod peninsula in Massachusetts, where the original recipe was created.
Traditionally it is aged for 2–4 weeks, which gives it its distinctive aroma.
Cape Cod pairs especially well with seafood such as lobster and shrimp.
It is produced by small family farms, ensuring high‑quality milk.
The original recipe includes a touch of sea salt to accentuate the flavor.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium in the cheese supports strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Cape Cod provides complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The cheese contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for the nervous system and metabolism.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Fermentation creates beneficial bacteria that help maintain gut health.

items.title: Low in lactose
items.content: Extended aging reduces lactose levels, making the cheese more tolerable for those with mild intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may experience reactions when consuming the cheese.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The cheese contains a notable amount of salt; individuals with hypertension should limit portions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of its fat content, excessive consumption can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Pathogen risk
items.content: Improper storage can allow harmful bacteria such as Listeria to grow.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice Cape Cod thinly for sandwiches, crumble it into salads, melt it in casseroles, or serve it with fruit and nuts. It melts well, making it a popular choice for sauces and pizza toppings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cheese in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C. For longer storage (over 2 weeks), wrap it in wax paper followed by aluminum foil to prevent drying out. Discard any cheese that develops mold other than the natural white rind.
